propositions: The snapshot janitor's reclaim trigger (DEFAULT_FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES = 2 GiB absolute) is disk-size-blind and unreachable on a 30-GiB volume, engaging only at 93.3% used, above both the 85% alarm floor and the 90% incident peak.

The snapshot store materializes full ~620 MiB copies of the ticket tree for each review, keyed on a ref advancing every ~26 seconds with minimal delta, creating ~0.85 GiB per review or 4.4 GiB/h growth on the container writable layer.

Adding a volume-relative headroom term (free_watermark_pct) to the janitor's trigger, combined with hysteresis that reclaims to a target margin above the trigger, makes the janitor engage before the alarm floor on small volumes.
The fix must store the new knob as an integer to survive the existing int-only config seam (_snapshot_int coerces with int()), and defaults to 0 (off) to leave existing deployments unchanged.
Live/grace snapshot entries must be preserved during reclaim, and the repaired path must engage at the 85% alarm floor on a 30-GiB volume where pre-fix it never engaged anywhere from 69% to 90%.
